description: The size of the dataset is given differently in each source. The data page says "2000+" CT scans and "19,562" questions. Codabench gives 2,088 cases (1,288 training, 400 validation, 400 test). The design document says 2,300 cases (1,500, 300 and 500), with about 4 questions per case. The released files hold 1,687 cases (1,287 training, 400 validation) and 16,538 questions. The questions are on 1,590 cases, with a median of 10 per case, and 97 cases have none. The design document describes 8 question skills, while the files have 6 types. It also promises gender and age, which the files do not have. Codabench lists data changes and deletions on 9 June 2024.
inspectedScope: Both JSON files, all rows; the data page; Codabench "Home" and "Dataset" pages; design document pp. 2, 11, 12 and 26.
detection: Counting cases and questions in the files and comparing them with each source.
impact: Readers who take the published numbers at face value expect more cases, more questions and demographic fields than the release holds.
handling: Use the counts of the released files, and cite the release version when reporting them.

description: Both JSON headers announce 400 test cases ("numTest": 400), but the "testing" list is empty and the Drive folder has no test images. Only training and validation cases are public.
inspectedScope: Both JSON headers and their "testing" lists; the Drive folder file list.
detection: Reading the header and the split lists, and listing the folder.
impact: Results on the challenge test set cannot be reproduced, so published challenge scores cannot be compared with new models.
handling: Report results on the validation set and say that the test set is not public.

description: amos_7008, amos_7312 and amos_7333 are in both imagesTr.zip and imagesVa.zip, with the same size and CRC32. The JSON files list all three as validation cases only.
inspectedScope: All 1,690 members of the two zips (from the file list, without opening the files) and both JSON files.

evidence.locator: file names in both zips; split of each case in the JSON

detection: Matching member names, sizes and CRC32 between the zips and with the JSON splits.
impact: Treating every file of imagesTr.zip as training data puts these 3 validation CTs into training.
handling: Take the split from the JSON files, not from the zip a file came from.

description: 4 cases name an MRI scanner model in their metadata: amos_6633 (SIGNA HDe) and amos_6665, amos_6927 and amos_6951 (Prisma). The design document lists only 5 CT scanner models. The 2 of these files in the local sample, amos_6633 and amos_6927, hold CT values (minimum −1,024), so their scanner field looks wrong.
inspectedScope: The scanner field of all 1,687 cases; voxel values of 2 local files (sample); design document p. 11.
detection: Counting scanner values and reading the voxel range of the local files.
impact: Grouping or filtering by scanner treats these CT scans as MRI.
handling: Do not rely on the scanner field for these 4 cases. Check the image values instead.

description: 2 CTs are stored as stacks of non-axial slices: amos_5693 as coronal slices (orientation LSP) and amos_5553 as sagittal slices (PSR). They are the only 2 cases with a 768 × 998 matrix in the metadata.
inspectedScope: The shape field of all 1,687 cases; orientation of both files, which are in the local sample.

evidence.locator: meta.shape of all cases; NIfTI affine of both files

detection: Listing in-plane matrix sizes and reading the orientation codes from the NIfTI header.
impact: Code that takes the third array axis as axial cuts these scans in the wrong direction.
handling: Reorient every scan by the orientation in its NIfTI header before use.

description: The licence statements disagree. Both JSON headers say CC BY-ND 4.0. The design document says the data follow "the CC BY-SA (Attribution-ShareAlike) adopted by AMOS22", and the data page states no licence. For the 228 CTs that are AMOS22 files, AMOS22's Zenodo record says CC BY 4.0, its dataset.json "CC-BY-SA 4.0" and the AMOS paper CC BY-NC-SA. During the challenge, the application form also made applicants promise to "obey the rules, NOT share the dataset", although the data are now in a public folder.
inspectedScope: Both JSON headers; design document pp. 8 and 22; the data page; Codabench "Rules" and "Instructions" pages and the application form; AMOS22 Zenodo record and dataset.json; AMOS paper Appendix B.3.
detection: Reading the licence statement of each source.
impact: It is unclear whether modified copies (ND) and commercial use (NC) are allowed, which matters for derived datasets and for this catalog's preview.
handling: Ask the provider which licence applies. Until then, follow the most restrictive statement.

description: Only 228 of the 1,687 CT files are AMOS22's own files (the amos_0xxx names). Another 1,377 files reuse AMOS22 file names but are different files. Of these, 1,091 have the names of AMOS22 unlabelled CTs (amos_5000 to amos_6899). The other 286 have the names of AMOS22 unlabelled MRI scans (amos_7xxx), although they hold CT. The 2 such files in the local sample have CT values. The remaining 82 names are not in AMOS22.
inspectedScope: All members of the two AMOS-MM zips compared with the AMOS22 zip listings by name, size and CRC32 (from the file lists, without opening the files).

evidence.locator: same name, different size or CRC32

detection: Comparing name, size and CRC32 of every file with the AMOS22 listings.
impact: When AMOS-MM is joined with AMOS22 by file name, different scans are paired and AMOS22 MRI scans are attached to AMOS-MM CT reports.
handling: Match the two datasets by file content (size and CRC32, or a hash), not by name. Only the amos_0xxx files are shared.
